approach: Add athena-core module host_rules.rs. It takes a gh::Runner, owner and repo. For each of athena/records and main it runs `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}`. That is a plain GET: no --method and no -f/-F/--input arguments. The reply is parsed as a JSON list of rule objects and mapped to three tri-state results (InForce, NotInForce, Unknown) per branch. A runner error or bad JSON makes every rule on that branch Unknown. The module renders a plain-text report that states it sees rulesets only. Register the module in lib.rs. Add a small GET-args helper in gh.rs. Update CHANGELOG and records-history.md §10 item 1 (job 1, part 3).

decisions.choice: The module calls Runner::gh directly with args ["api", path], built by a new pub helper in gh.rs (gh::get_args). It does not use GhClient::api.
decisions.reason: GhClient::api_text always adds `--method <m>` and its retry and error-log loop is tied to HostOperation. Criterion 3 requires no method override, and gh api defaults to GET. The helper keeps the argument shape in one place, next to the other api calls.

rejected.why: It passes `--method GET`, which breaks the no-override assertion, and it needs a HostOperation variant in athena-data.
It returns 403 here, and reading classic protection is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Three-state enum RuleState {InForce, NotInForce, Unknown}. Any error or parse failure gives Unknown for all three rules on that branch. A reply that is valid JSON but not an array is also Unknown.
decisions.reason: A failed read must never be taken as 'not in force' or 'in force'.

decisions.choice: The same three-rule evaluation applies to both branches. Up-to-date required is in force only when a required_status_checks rule has parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy == true. If several such rules exist, any strict one counts.
decisions.reason: This is the stated mapping. The check stays symmetric and simple, and the report names all three rules per branch.

rejected.option: Check only the rules each branch needs (force-push and deletion on athena/records, up-to-date on main)
rejected.why: The criteria want all three rules named per branch, so Sri sees the full picture.

decisions.choice: The report and the module doc both state that only rulesets are seen and classic branch protection is not visible.
decisions.reason: This answers the earlier finding, and a 'not in force' result could otherwise be misread as 'unprotected'.

files.purpose: Host-rules check (D111, records-history §3, part 3 of job 1): the RuleState and BranchRules types, check(runner, owner, repo), the JSON evaluation, the report renderer, and the tests.
Add `pub mod host_rules;` in alphabetical order, after `gh`.
Add pub fn get_args(path) -> Vec<String> returning ["api", path], with a doc note that gh api defaults to GET.
Add an entry under [Unreleased] ### Added. It describes the read-only host-rules check, cites records-history §3 and §10, and states the rulesets-only limit.

In §10 item 1, note that the host-rules confirmation is done by the read-only check in host_rules.rs. It sees rulesets only, so classic branch protection is not visible and Sri must set the §3 rules as rulesets.

steps: Read the Runner trait and GhFailure in gh.rs. Add get_args(path) to gh.rs.

Create host_rules.rs. Give it a //! doc citing D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3, calling it part 3 of job 1 and stating that only rulesets are seen. Define the Rule enum or constants, RuleState, BranchRules, and fn check(runner: &dyn Runner, owner, repo) -> Vec<BranchRules> over ["athena/records", "main"]. Define fn evaluate(reply: &str) -> [RuleState; 3] and fn render(&[BranchRules]) -> String.
Write the tests with a RecordingRunner (RefCell<Vec<Vec<String>>> plus a queue of Result<String>), covering criteria 1-5.
Add the CHANGELOG entry citing §3 and §10, and the records-history §10 item 1 note.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Record each command, its exit status and its output tail in the evidence.

risks.risk: Sri reads 'not in force' as 'branch unprotected' when classic protection is on.
risks.mitigation: A rules/branches reply lists only the rules that apply to the branch, including those inherited from org-level rulesets. The report and docs say 'rulesets only'. Classic protection is never reported as in force.

risks.risk: The API shape differs slightly, for example the parameters key is missing.
risks.mitigation: Parse leniently, and treat any reply that is not a JSON array as Unknown. Skip array items that lack a string `type`.

risks.risk: The evidence for criterion 7 is weak again.
risks.mitigation: Run the fmt, clippy and test commands, and quote each with its exit status and output tail.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests with a fake Runner that returns canned rules/branches JSON: a list with non_fast_forward and deletion for athena/records, and one with required_status_checks (strict true) for main.
demonstrations.observes: Check results give force-push forbidden and deletion forbidden InForce on athena/records, and up-to-date required InForce on main.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the mapping from non_fast_forward, deletion and strict required_status_checks to in-force states were missing, the asserts on the fixture replies would fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests for `[]`, strict false, strict absent, and a list with only non_fast_forward.
demonstrations.observes: `[]` gives all three NotInForce. Strict false or absent gives up-to-date NotInForce. The partial list gives force-push InForce and deletion NotInForce.
demonstrations.fails_without: If absent rules defaulted to in force, or the strict flag was ignored, these asserts would fail.

demonstrations.method: A recording fake Runner stores every args vector.
demonstrations.observes: Exactly two calls: ["api","repos/o/r/rules/branches/athena/records"] and ["api","repos/o/r/rules/branches/main"]. No arg is --method, -f, -F or --input, and none contains "protection".
demonstrations.fails_without: If the code used --method, -f, --input or the /protection path, the recorded-args assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: A fake Runner returns Err(GhFailure with status 403), Err(GhFailure with status 503), and Ok("not json"). One test also covers a failure on one branch only.
demonstrations.observes: All three rules on the affected branch are Unknown. The other branch still gets its own result.
demonstrations.fails_without: If errors or bad JSON were mapped to NotInForce (or InForce), the Unknown asserts would fail.

demonstrations.method: A test renders the report and checks its text.
demonstrations.observes: The report contains lines such as 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force', one line for each of the 3 rules on each of the 2 branches (including 'unknown' lines), and a sentence that only rulesets are seen and classic branch protection is not.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the report omitted a rule or the rulesets-only note, the string asserts would fail.

demonstrations.method: Read the //! doc in host_rules.rs, `pub mod host_rules;` in lib.rs, and the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] ### Added entry. The test run shows the module compiled in.
demonstrations.observes: The doc cites D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3 and says 'part 3 of job 1'. The CHANGELOG entry cites §3 and §10. lib.rs lists the module, and the host_rules tests run under athena-core.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the module were not registered, the tests above would not be compiled or run, so this command would show no host_rules tests.

demonstrations.method: The producer runs `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` from the repo root, and quotes each command with its exit status and last output lines.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0 and the evidence cites each command as run.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lint, format or test regression anywhere in the workspace would give a non-zero exit.

open_questions: How the owner and repo are supplied is left to the caller, because CLI wiring is out of scope. The function takes them as arguments.
Whether gh api returns the rules/branches reply as a plain list at the current API version is assumed from the brief. It was not checked against the live host.
